reason: Measured at 390 in state=day with the disclosure forced open. The geometry the finding reports is broadly right and round 7's half is confirmed working: data-px=2, measure 640px, ticks at 34/62/76/90/118/132 (six inside 98px), pushes 21/56/91/112/147, and every numeral sits beside its own words (14, 28, 35, 42, 56, 63 each pair correctly with their title and mono date). But the finding is wrong about what it means and its fix is the wrong trade. Three things kill it. (1) The headline is false. The 'Behind you' disclosure is CLOSED by default; the screen the audience opens on the wedding morning says MARA & FINN / Today / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day, and states the past in one sentence, 'Venue walk-through, 19 September.' The rail is opt-in, so it is not 'the screen's one piece of substance' and a reader who never opens it is untouched. It also miscounts its own evidence: five rows come back data-crowded=true, not six (the five pushes it lists are exactly the five). (2) Nothing here is illegible or misassigned. Every row carries its distance as a numeral, its date in mono and its title, correctly paired, and at 3x the tick cluster resolves as six separate 7px rings on 14px pitch, not a blur. What the finding objects to is that a true scale puts six marks close together and leaves three rows without a mark beside their words. That is a density artefact of an honest measure, not a misstatement; no reader is told anything false. The leader criticism is geometrically correct (all five draw at x=90, on the rail, and overlap into one continuous stretch from 65 to 282, so no individual leader can be traced) but a leader that merges into the rail is a no-op, not a harm, and the code comment already reasons about why a 157px vertical in a 20px gutter cannot be moved off the rail. (3) The proposed fix makes the screen decisively worse and abandons the direction's central claim on the one rail that most rewards it. Evenly spacing the back rows destroys the two gaps that ARE legible and are the emotional payload of the wedding morning: 'The Orchard reserved' at 336px, 173px of empty rail, then 'We said yes' at 548px. The finding calls that empty stretch a defect ('170px of rail carries nothing at all') when it is the sentence the screen exists to say - you said yes nine months ago, and then nothing for half a year. Flattening it to a 49px row pitch converts the day-of past back into the dated .b-behindRows table the direction deliberately replaced on this screen, and lets the numeral do a job position was supposed to do, which is precisely the trade the lock forbids. Refuted: factually overstated, and the fix would make it worse.
sharpenedFix: Nothing here is worth a change at the 9.5 bar. If anyone still wants to spend polish on the knot, the only move that stays inside the lock is to leave every top and every tick exactly where it is and give the leader a job it can actually do - e.g. reveal a single row's leader at fore-62 on :hover/:focus-within of .b-back .b-item, so the mark-to-row pairing is answerable on demand instead of five leaders painting one stretch of rail at rest. That is a two-line CSS addition, changes no position, and needs no new colour. It is optional; the rail is not broken without it.
